title: Dyslipidaemia: Statin Initiation and Lipid Targets

evidenceAudit.scope: Adults being considered for or taking lipid-lowering treatment in primary care: who to offer a statin, dose and targets for primary and secondary prevention, repeat testing, intolerance and escalation, and specialist referral thresholds. Checked against NICE NG238 recommendations 1.1, 1.4–1.12. Medicine-pathway restructure on 2026-10-18: medicines regrouped into branches, steps and give-all vs choose-one options; no dose, source or clinical claim was re-checked.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 14 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.

Medicine list restructured into a branched decision pathway on 2026-10-18. Doses, routes, adjustments, monitoring, contraindications and sources are unchanged from authoring-standard-2026-10-14-v2-investigations-live.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi national lipid guideline was opened for this version; thresholds and doses are NICE NG238. The repository's cardiovascular-risk topic cites the Saudi Clinical Preventive Guideline, which was not re-opened here.
QRISK3 is a UK-derived tool; its calibration in the Saudi population was not assessed.
Medicine doses were reused from the repository's earlier lipid topic (NICE NG238 and FDA labels) and were not re-opened on 14 Oct 2026.
SFDA registration and hospital formulary availability were not independently verified.

Medicine pathway: branch entry criteria, preferred options and “use when” conditions were assigned from this topic's own indications and management steps. Confirm each against the cited guideline before clinical use.

pathophysiology.summary: Raised non-HDL cholesterol drives atherosclerosis; any statin at any dose reduces cardiovascular risk (NG238 1.9.4). Benefit depends on absolute risk: a 10-year QRISK3 score of 10% or more triggers an atorvastatin offer for primary prevention (NG238 1.6.7). People with established cardiovascular disease are offered high-intensity atorvastatin whatever their cholesterol (NG238 1.7.2). Common secondary causes (excess alcohol, uncontrolled diabetes, hypothyroidism, liver disease, nephrotic syndrome) must be excluded and treated before specialist referral or statin start (NG238 1.4.3, 1.6.6). Statins are contraindicated in pregnancy because of risk to the unborn child (NG238 1.5.9).

symptoms: Usually none; most people are found by cardiovascular risk assessment (NG238 1.1).
Persistent generalised unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness, before or during statin treatment (NG238 1.5.7, 1.11.3).
physicalSigns: Blood pressure, BMI and smoking status for baseline assessment (NG238 1.5.5).
Clinical findings and family history suggesting a familial lipid disorder (NG238 1.4.2).
redFlags: Triglycerides above 20 mmol/L not due to alcohol or poor glycaemic control: urgent specialist review (NG238 1.4.6).
Total cholesterol above 9.0 mmol/L or non-HDL cholesterol above 7.5 mmol/L: specialist assessment even without a family history (NG238 1.4.5).
Creatine kinase above 5 times the upper limit of normal twice, 7 days apart: do not start a statin (NG238 1.5.7).
Pregnancy possible: stop the statin; stop 3 months before trying to conceive; restart only after breastfeeding (NG238 1.5.10).
precipitants: Excess alcohol, uncontrolled diabetes, hypothyroidism, liver disease or nephrotic syndrome (NG238 1.4.3).
Medicines that cause dyslipidaemia, such as immunosuppressants (NG238 1.1.10).
Interacting drugs, grapefruit juice and some supplements raise statin adverse-effect risk (NG238 1.5.4).

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Judge from clinical findings, a full lipid profile and family history, not cut-offs alone; use the NICE familial hypercholesterolaemia guideline (NG238 1.4.2, 1.4.4).
Treat the cause first: alcohol, diabetes, hypothyroidism, liver disease, nephrotic syndrome (NG238 1.4.3).
Creatine kinase below 5 times the upper limit of normal: unlikely statin-related; explore other causes (NG238 1.11.4).

ruleIn.testName: Full lipid profile (total cholesterol, HDL, non-HDL, triglycerides)
ruleIn.modalityTarget: Adult being assessed for lipid-lowering treatment
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Total cholesterol above 9.0 mmol/L or non-HDL above 7.5 mmol/L: specialist assessment; triglycerides above 20 mmol/L: urgent review (NG238 1.4.5–1.4.6).
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Measure total and HDL cholesterol for the best risk estimate; repeat 2–3 months after starting or changing treatment (NG238 1.4.1, 1.11.1).
ruleIn.normalValue: Total cholesterol below 5.2 mmol/L (200 mg/dL); LDL below 3.4 mmol/L (130 mg/dL); triglycerides below 1.7 mmol/L (150 mg/dL); local ranges apply

references.title: NICE NG238: Cardiovascular disease: risk assessment and reduction, including lipid modification

ruleIn.modalityTarget: Adult aged 25–84 without CVD, including type 2 diabetes
ruleIn.expectedFinding: 10% or more: offer atorvastatin 20 mg after an informed discussion (NG238 1.6.7).
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Use QRISK3 rather than QRISK2 for people on corticosteroids or atypical antipsychotics or with lupus, migraine, severe mental illness or erectile dysfunction (NG238 1.1.7–1.1.8).

references.title: NICE NG238: Cardiovascular disease: risk assessment and reduction, including lipid modification

ruleIn.testName: Baseline liver transaminase and renal function
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Transaminases raised but below 3 times the upper limit of normal do not exclude statin treatment (NG238 1.5.6).
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Also record smoking, alcohol, blood pressure, BMI, diabetes status and, if thyroid symptoms, TSH (NG238 1.5.5). Repeat transaminase at 12 months only (NG238 1.11.2).
ruleIn.normalValue: ALT and AST within the local reference range; eGFR 60 mL/min/1.73 m² or more

references.title: NICE NG238: Cardiovascular disease: risk assessment and reduction, including lipid modification

ruleIn.testName: Baseline assessment before a statin: smoking, alcohol, blood pressure, BMI and diabetes status
ruleIn.modalityTarget: Clinical assessment and baseline blood tests
ruleIn.targetCondition: Modifiable risk factors and contraindications to statin treatment
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Risk factors present that raise cardiovascular risk or alter treatment choice
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Record all of these with the full lipid profile, renal function and transaminase before starting. Check TSH only if there are symptoms of an underactive or overactive thyroid.
ruleIn.normalValue: Individual targets agreed with the patient

references.title: NICE NG238: Cardiovascular disease: risk assessment and reduction, including lipid modification

ruleOut.modalityTarget: Adult with persistent unexplained muscle symptoms
ruleOut.expectedFinding: More than 5 times the upper limit of normal: repeat after 7 days and do not start if still above; raised but below 5 times: start a lower dose (NG238 1.5.7).
ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Measure only if symptoms occur; do not measure in asymptomatic people (NG238 1.11.3, 1.11.5).
ruleOut.normalValue: Below the laboratory upper limit of normal (about 200 U/L in many assays; varies with sex and activity). A statin is withheld if CK stays above 5 times that limit on repeat testing

references.title: NICE NG238: Cardiovascular disease: risk assessment and reduction, including lipid modification

ruleOut.modalityTarget: Adult with triglycerides 10–20 mmol/L on a non-fasting test
ruleOut.expectedFinding: Repeat fasting after 5 days but within 2 weeks; seek specialist advice if still above 10 mmol/L (NG238 1.4.7).
ruleOut.clinicalRationale: At 4.5–9.9 mmol/L risk may be underestimated: optimise other risk factors (NG238 1.4.8).

references.title: NICE NG238: Cardiovascular disease: risk assessment and reduction, including lipid modification

ruleOut.testName: Thyroid-stimulating hormone and screen for other secondary causes
ruleOut.modalityTarget: Venous TSH, with alcohol history, HbA1c, liver tests and urine protein
ruleOut.targetCondition: Secondary dyslipidaemia (hypothyroidism, excess alcohol, uncontrolled diabetes, liver disease, nephrotic syndrome)
ruleOut.expectedFinding: Raised TSH or another secondary cause explaining the lipid result
ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Exclude common secondary causes before specialist referral. Refer for specialist assessment if total cholesterol is above 9.0 mmol/L or non-HDL cholesterol is above 7.5 mmol/L, even without a family history.
ruleOut.normalValue: TSH about 0.4–4.0 mIU/L (typical adult range; local range applies)

references.title: NICE NG238: Cardiovascular disease: risk assessment and reduction, including lipid modification

ruleOut.modalityTarget: Clinical findings, full lipid profile and family history
ruleOut.expectedFinding: A familial pattern is judged from clinical findings, lipid profile and family history, not from strict cut-offs alone
ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Use the NICE familial hypercholesterolaemia guideline to decide whether to suspect and how to treat it.
ruleOut.normalValue: No family history of premature cardiovascular disease; lipid profile below the thresholds that prompt referral

references.title: NICE NG238: Cardiovascular disease: risk assessment and reduction, including lipid modification

clinicalManagement.title: Identify and assess risk
actions: Use QRISK3 for ages 25–84 without CVD; do not use a tool in type 1 diabetes, eGFR below 60 mL/min/1.73 m² or albuminuria, or familial hypercholesterolaemia (NG238 1.1.7–1.1.9).
Tools may underestimate risk in HIV, severe mental illness, autoimmune disease and people on immunosuppressants; age 85 or over is increased risk by age alone (NG238 1.1.10–1.1.11).

clinicalManagement.title: Prepare before offering a statin
actions: Discuss benefits and risks; the risk of muscle symptoms is small and rhabdomyolysis is extremely rare (NG238 1.5.1–1.5.3).
Do baseline tests, exclude and treat secondary causes, ask about muscle symptoms, and check pregnancy potential (NG238 1.5.5–1.5.10, 1.6.6).
Primary prevention: discuss lifestyle first, reassess risk after lifestyle change, and offer a statin if lifestyle is ineffective or inappropriate (NG238 1.6.2–1.6.5).

clinicalManagement.title: Start the statin
actions: Primary prevention: atorvastatin 20 mg if 10-year QRISK3 is 10% or more; consider 20 mg at 85 or over; type 1 diabetes and CKD also atorvastatin 20 mg (NG238 1.6.7, 1.6.9, 1.6.12, 1.8.1).
Secondary prevention: atorvastatin 80 mg whatever the cholesterol unless a lower dose is needed; do not delay, and discuss lifestyle at the same time (NG238 1.7.2–1.7.4).
Acute coronary syndrome: start without delay; full lipid profile on admission and at 2–3 months (NG238 1.7.5).

clinicalManagement.title: Recheck and optimise
actions: Measure transaminase and a full lipid profile at 2–3 months; transaminase again at 12 months only (NG238 1.11.1–1.11.2).
Target not met: discuss adherence and dose timing, reinforce lifestyle, and consider a higher-intensity or maximum tolerated dose (NG238 1.9.1).
In CKD with eGFR 30 mL/min/1.73 m² or more increase the atorvastatin dose; agree higher doses with a renal specialist below 30 (NG238 1.8.2–1.8.3).

clinicalManagement.title: Intolerance and escalation
actions: High-intensity adverse effects: stop and retry after symptoms settle, switch to rosuvastatin if on atorvastatin, reduce the dose, or use a lower-intensity statin; aim for the maximum tolerated dose (NG238 1.9.2–1.9.3).
Statins contraindicated or not tolerated at any dose: ezetimibe (secondary prevention, whatever the cholesterol) (NG238 1.10.3; primary prevention 1.10.1).

Secondary prevention not at target on maximum statin: consider alirocumab, evolocumab, ezetimibe or inclisiran per NICE technology appraisals; consider ezetimibe with a statin even if the target is met (NG238 1.7.9–1.7.10).

clinicalManagement.title: Annual review
actions: Annual medicines review; annual full lipid profile for secondary prevention and consider it for primary prevention (NG238 1.11.8–1.11.10).
Do not stop a statin because of a rise in glucose or HbA1c (NG238 1.11.6).
Do not routinely offer fibrates, nicotinic acid, bile acid sequestrants or omega-3 compounds (icosapent ethyl only as in TA805) (NG238 1.12.2–1.12.7).

clinicalManagement.title: Specialist referral
actions: Total cholesterol above 9.0 mmol/L or non-HDL above 7.5 mmol/L: specialist assessment (NG238 1.4.5).
Triglycerides above 20 mmol/L not due to alcohol or poor glycaemic control: urgent review; 10–20 mmol/L: repeat fasting and refer if still above 10 (NG238 1.4.6–1.4.7).
Suspected familial hypercholesterolaemia: follow the NICE familial hypercholesterolaemia guideline (NG238 1.4.4).

contraindications: Acute liver failure or decompensated cirrhosis

medicationPlan.note: Atorvastatin 20 mg and 80 mg doses are NICE NG238 recommendations; rosuvastatin and ezetimibe doses are from the repository's earlier label-checked topic. Atorvastatin below 80 mg for secondary prevention was off-label use in December 2023 (NG238 1.7.3). SFDA registration was not verified. Check hospital formulary.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: 10-year QRISK3 score of 10% or more (aged 25–84 without CVD); also CKD (NG238 1.6.7, 1.8.1); do not rule out below 10% if informed preference or risk may be underestimated (1.6.8)
More than 40% reduction in non-HDL cholesterol (NG238 1.6.1)
Any established CVD, whatever the cholesterol, unless interactions, high adverse-effect risk or preference favour a lower dose (NG238 1.7.2–1.7.3)
LDL cholesterol 2.0 mmol/L or less, or non-HDL cholesterol 2.6 mmol/L or less (NG238 1.7.1)
Older than 40 years, diabetes for more than 10 years, established nephropathy or other CVD risk factors; start atorvastatin 20 mg (NG238 1.6.10, 1.6.12)

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Type 1 diabetes, eGFR below 60 mL/min/1.73 m² or albuminuria, familial hypercholesterolaemia (NG238 1.1.9)

teaching.scope: Adults being considered for or taking lipid-lowering treatment in primary care: who to offer a statin, dose and targets for primary and secondary prevention, repeat testing, intolerance and escalation, and specialist referral thresholds. Checked against NICE NG238 recommendations 1.1, 1.4–1.12.
learningObjectives: Offer the right statin dose for primary and secondary prevention and name the lipid targets.
Know the lipid thresholds that need specialist referral.
pitfalls: Stopping a statin because HbA1c or glucose rose.
Measuring creatine kinase in people with no muscle symptoms.
Using a risk tool in type 1 diabetes, CKD or familial hypercholesterolaemia.
keyPoints: Primary prevention: atorvastatin 20 mg at 10-year QRISK3 of 10% or more; secondary prevention: atorvastatin 80 mg.
Targets: non-HDL fall of more than 40% (primary); LDL 2.0 mmol/L or less or non-HDL 2.6 mmol/L or less (secondary).
Any statin at any dose reduces risk, so aim for the maximum tolerated dose.

patientEducation: Explain that the risk of muscle pain is small and severe muscle damage is extremely rare (NG238 1.5.3).
Advise to report unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness and to check interactions before new drugs or supplements (NG238 1.5.4, 1.11.3).
lifestyleAndDiet: Eat 30% or less of energy as fat and 7% or less as saturated fat, replacing saturated with unsaturated fats (NG238 1.3.2).
Be active, stop smoking and manage weight (NG238 1.3.5, 1.3.9, 1.3.11).
Do not advise plant stanols or sterols to prevent CVD (NG238 1.3.12).
mdtReferrals: Specialist lipid service for the referral thresholds above.
Renal specialist for higher statin doses with eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m² (NG238 1.8.3).
Weight management or exercise referral schemes for lifestyle support (NG238 1.6.3).
dischargeCriteria: Statin started with the discussion documented and baseline tests done.
Repeat lipid profile and transaminase booked at 2–3 months.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Lipid profile and transaminase at 2–3 months; transaminase at 12 months; annual medicines review with a full lipid profile (NG238 1.11.1–1.11.10).
